text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: high error rate (502/504) and elevated p99 latency for inference routes serving org_id=stormguard. Alerts: qps spike from 120 -> 3.2k in 3m, kernel OOMs reported. Incident created: INC-20260317-89 :rotating_light:
oncall-mike: On it. grabbing logs and verifying. assigning to SRE.
sre-jamie: I'm looking. traces show sustained long tail on /v1/generate for that org only. backend queue backlog increasing.
sre-jamie: customer traffic pattern shows a sudden burst of long-context requests (seq_len ~ 4096) plus repeated retries.
eng-runtime-lead: If they're blowing up kv cache size we'll start evictions; temp mitigation options: 1) org-level rate cap drop 2) deprioritize org (qos) 3) spike route to smaller model 4) emergency quota bump for their bursty service users. Which direction do we want?
oncall-mike: What's current org RL?
sre-jamie: Org RL = 250 QPS. They hit 3.2k.
sre-jamie: Immediate goal: protect cluster from node OOMs; also avoid customer 5xx if possible. My vote: apply temporary hard cap at 600 QPS and enable token-bucket smoothing for that org, plus selectively route non-critical model calls to a lower-capacity model.
eng-runtime-lead: Agree. smoothing + downroute non-critical models gives room. Need approval for the cap change from Product/CS because it affects customer throughput.
support-linda: CS is on the line with StormGuard; they're seeing timeouts for their premium workspace. They're asking for an emergency unblock. If we cut, they lose throughput; if we raise we risk platform stability.
cs-ashley: From CS: they can fallback some internal batch jobs for 30m, but their web-facing customers are premium and must be kept online. They request a temporary increase to 1000 QPS for their "live-monitor" org key only, not all users.
sre-jamie: Proposal: 1) Create a targeted override for API key(s) tagged "live-monitor" inside org stormguard to +1000 QPS, TTL 30m, with server-side smoothing and concurrency cap at 50. 2) For rest of org, apply hard cap 600 QPS. 3) Route heavy long-context calls for that org to model-compact-1 (smaller) unless call contains header X-critical: true.
oncall-mike: I can implement. Will perform change via admin API and post diffs.
eng-runtime-lead: Make sure to flip on request sampling so we can audit regressions. Also set rollback timer to 30 min.
sre-jamie: Commands ready — run these in admin console (examples):
```
# set org default cap
PUT /admin/orgs/stormguard/rate_limit {"qps":600, "burst":1200}
# add key-scoped override
PUT /admin/keys/sg-live-monitor/rate_limit {"qps":1000, "burst":2000, "ttl":1800}
# set routing rule
POST /admin/routing/overrides {"org":"stormguard","from_model":"model-xl","to_model":"model-compact-1","condition":"!header.X-critical"}
```

oncall-mike: Applying now. will update once changes propagate (approx 30s). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
incident-bot: deploybot: policy update applied by mike (id:upd-5532). Propagation to edge in 22s.
oncall-mike: Propagated. Initial metrics: total org QPS dropped from 3.2k -> 1.1k. Errors decreased from 18% -> 4%. Node memory pressure easing.
sre-jamie: Good. sampling shows the live-monitor key latency is stable under 300ms with concurrency limit. Other org traffic queued down as expected.
support-linda: CS update: StormGuard engineering acknowledges partial unblock for their premium flows. They're seeing degraded but acceptable performance. Asking for ETA on full recovery.
eng-runtime-lead: We'll watch for 15m, if stable we can relax caps gradually. Also schedule follow-up to examine why they retried; recommend prom-level mitigations and client backoff.
cs-ashley: I'll relay to the customer and schedule a postmortem. They want a call in 2 hours to discuss long-term rate limits and burst allowances.
incident-bot: Reminder: rollback timer set for 1800s. Next check-in in 10m.
sre-jamie: Monitoring looks OK at T+10. p50/p95 stable, no new OOMs.
oncall-mike: Starting a gradual relax: bump org default to 800 QPS, key override remains 1000.
incident-bot: policy update applied by mike (id:upd-5533).
sre-jamie: After relax, org QPS at 1.6k, errors 2.1%, node mem stable.
sre-jamie: I'll keep the incident open for another hour and will hand off in the next shift.
oncall-mike: Leaving notes: actions taken + commands + rollback ids. handoff to oncall-next. :white_check_mark:
eng-runtime-lead: Follow-up actions assigned: (1) post-incident RCA on why long-context retries triggered OOM (owner: eng-runtime), (2) consider client-side SDK backoff improvements (owner: devex), (3) customer-specific burst policy proposal (owner: product).
cs-ashley: Customer call scheduled. thanked the team.
incident-bot: incident INC-20260317-89 status: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned to sleuth for RCA.
sre-jamie: Handoff: next oncall please watch org stormguard p95 and KV eviction counts. I'm reachable if it flares.
oncall-mike: handed off to oncall-next. closing my active console session.
support-linda: Logging an internal support ticket for billing/credits discussion since we applied a partial cap and key override.
eng-runtime-lead: Good work. Postmortem doc link will be added to the incident once RCA is ready. :memo:
